Create a clean, professional, trust-first website for VoltBay.

Tone & Style:
- Professional
- Honest
- Calm
- Early-stage but credible
- No hype words, no exaggeration
- No marketing fluff

Target Audience:
- EV users in India
- Small & medium EV charging station owners
- Non-technical users

========================================
HERO SECTION
========================================

Headline:
VoltBay — Smarter EV Charging, Without Waiting

Subtext:
VoltBay helps EV users book charging slots in advance
and helps charging station owners manage demand efficiently.

Status Note (important, visible):
VoltBay is currently in early access and limited testing.

========================================
WHAT VOLTBAY DOES
========================================

Section Title:
How VoltBay Helps

Two-column layout:

For EV Users:
- Find nearby EV charging stations
- Book time slots before arriving
- Reduce waiting time and uncertainty

For Station Owners:
- Manage bookings digitally
- Reduce crowding and idle time
- Serve customers more efficiently

Use simple language. Avoid technical terms.

========================================
TRY OUR ANDROID APP (APK)
========================================

Section Title:
Try Our Android App (Early Access)

Button Text:
Try Our APK

Button Action:
Open this link in a new tab:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1n58OZPh9hfD9xftpmr1hIKSLWBdnJYFR/view

Below the button (small text):
Early access Android APK.
Manual installation required.
Android devices only.
No payments are collected at this stage.

Optional helper text:
If you need help installing the app, please contact us.

========================================
OWNER ONBOARDING NOTE
========================================

Text Block:
Charging station onboarding is currently invite-only.
Please contact us before registering a station.
This helps us maintain quality, safety, and reliability.

========================================
ABOUT US
========================================

Section Title:
About VoltBay

Body Text:
VoltBay is being built as a practical solution to reduce
waiting, confusion, and inefficiency at EV charging stations in India.
The focus is on simple, reliable technology that solves real-world problems.

Founder:
Sathwik  
Student founder focused on building practical and honest EV infrastructure solutions.

Co-Founder:
Vinay  
Supports early testing, operations, and execution of the platform.

VoltBay is currently in its early development phase
and is being improved continuously based on real user feedback.

========================================
TRUST & TRANSPARENCY
========================================

Bullet Points:
- Built in India
- Early access testing version
- No payments required currently
- No fake promises or numbers
- Feedback-driven development

========================================
CONTACT & SUPPORT
========================================

Section Title:
Contact & Support

Text:
For feedback, support, or station onboarding inquiries:
myvoltbay@gmail.com

========================================
FOOTER
========================================

Footer Text:
VoltBay © 2026  
Early Access Version

**Developing Credible Content**

I'm focusing intently on crafting the website copy for VoltBay. The goal is a tone that's professional, trustworthy, and avoids any marketing jargon. Honesty and clarity are paramount as I shape the initial messaging, ensuring it resonates with a discerning audience. The challenge lies in communicating the value proposition of EV charging slot booking directly, without resorting to hyperbole.


**Prioritizing Website Structure**

I've been meticulously defining the website's structure. Key sections include a clear hero section, feature breakdowns for both users and station owners, and prominent app download links with accompanying disclaimers. I'm prioritizing user onboarding, especially for station owners, with an invite-only approach at launch. The "About" section will highlight the mission and founders, reinforcing trust. I am incorporating a support email contact and a copyright notice in the footer.


**Structuring the Layout**

I'm now fully immersed in the website's technical implementation. I've begun crafting the React components, from the `Navbar` to the `Footer`. Currently, I am designing the `Hero`, `Features`, `AppDownload`, `Onboarding`, `About`, `Trust`, and `Contact` sections, ensuring a professional and honest tone. I'm leveraging Tailwind for styling, React 18+ with `createRoot`, and TypeScript for type safety. Subtle CSS transitions will be used instead of `framer-motion` to maintain a calm aesthetic. I've opted for a high-contrast `Hero` headline with a prominent "Early Access" badge and simple icons for the `Features` section.


**Ensuring Clarity of Status**

I'm now implementing the "Early Access" notification. I've opted for a prominent badge in the `Hero` section to immediately inform visitors of our current development stage. This design choice aligns with my commitment to transparency and building trust, ensuring we communicate our current stage to users. I want the site to be calm with neutral colors and whitespace to keep the visual design balanced.

**Refining Import Strategies**

I'm now diving into the import strategies to troubleshoot this `useContext` error. The inconsistency between the `index.html` importmap and the `index.tsx` file is screaming at me. I'm scrutinizing the potential version conflicts within the imported dependencies, especially focusing on how `framer-motion` handles React internally. I'm considering using `?external=react` with `esm.sh` or enforcing a unified React version throughout the project to ensure `useContext` works as intended.


**Examining the React Context**

I've been honing in on the root cause of the `Cannot read properties of null` error, centering around `useContext`. I've realized that inconsistent React instances between `react-dom` and `react` are the prime suspects, and I'm now zeroing in on this. My current thoughts are that the import map might not be robust enough to manage the dependencies for framer-motion which might be bundling its own React instance. Let me double check my `index.tsx` import of `react-dom`.


**Pinpointing React Conflict**

I'm now certain the core issue is `framer-motion`'s use of a separate React instance. To resolve this, I'll update the import map. My plan involves forcing `framer-motion` to use the same React instance as the rest of the app. I'll make the import map more standard for ESM.sh, employing specific directives like `?external=react,react-dom` to enforce this. The structure will use the main entries for the `react` and `react-dom` dependencies.


**Refining the Import Map**

I'm now revising the import map to address the likely double-React issue, focusing on how `framer-motion` imports its dependencies. I'm prioritizing ensuring a unified React instance across the project, making it more robust. This includes using a unified import strategy and consolidating `react-dom` usage. I'm also ensuring the `metadata.json` is consistent. My approach now centers around using external directives in the import map.


**Applying the Import Map Fix**

I've just implemented the proposed fix for the double-React problem, which I strongly suspected. I've updated the import map to ensure that `framer-motion` uses the same React and React-DOM instances as the rest of the application. I've configured the import map with the necessary `external` directives, specifically focusing on unifying the React versions. My hope is that this will resolve the `Cannot read properties of null` error. I'm now testing the code.
